build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not module 0: its 921 packed bytes decode to $CA00-$CDE6 (the same on all four sides); the unpacker reads on to the end of its four-sector window, so these are the next stream's packed bytes decoded with module 0's table: module 1's on sides 1, 2 and 4 (this snapshot's), module 2's on side 3. Nothing reads them

comments.text: Module 0, the doctor (a clinic, infirmary or hospital: healing, an exam and cures for diseases); its own bytes are $CA00-$CDE6, the same on all four sides. The game's class-6 square handler loads and calls it for a record whose action byte is $80 ($8839-$884E); seven of the 42 map snapshots have such a record, each reached through a class-10 entrance square that turns itself into it when the party answers Y to "Enter new location (Y/N)?". The record at ($5F/$60): +0 $80; +1/+2 $FD $FD, which the game applies when the module returns (game $8840: LDA #1, JMP $B105, alter_square on the party's square; $FD puts back the entrance square kept in $AD/$AE and returns carry clear, which ends the game's square loop); +3 the map message shown as the greeting; +4 the price of one CON point; +5 the price of the exam; +6 the price of one cure (dollars, 0-255 each); +7..+$12 the name, 11 characters and a zero. Keeps the shown picture $AB and the animation flag $AC on the stack, copies the name over the location name at $F4D0, shows picture 0 from the buffer at $E000 (show_picture_e000 $041C, which prints that name under it) and goes on at doctor_ask.

Asks who is treated: redraws the roster (roster_show $02B7), offers the exam again (doctor_exam_flag = 1) and withdraws the cure and heal offers, prints the record's greeting (map message +3 through print_map_message $0317; the greetings open with code 7, which clears the text window) and "Who wants treatment?" (message 23), and waits for a member number (pick_member $02AE). Left-arrow goes to doctor_leave. Otherwise the number goes into doctor_patient, that roster line is highlighted (roster_line_highlight $02C9, which selects the member) and a member whose CON is exactly 0 (con_is_zero $02BD: dead, the roster's skull) gets "<name> is beyond my help." (message 9, then the (RETURN) wait of its code 6) and the question is asked again; anyone else goes to doctor_offer.

Leaves the doctor: pulls the animation flag $AC and the picture number $AB that doctor_start kept, unpacks the map's stream to $DE00-$EDFF again (unpack_map_stream $03C5; picture 0 was unpacked into the buffer at $E000, limit $F000, over part of it) and returns with carry set, which makes the game redraw the screen (game $8872 to $AC8C) before it applies the record's +1/+2.

Works out what the doctor offers the patient (the current character) and shows it. The LDA's operand is doctor_exam_flag: while an exam is on offer the disease byte is not looked at; once it has been paid for, a non-zero disease byte +$28 sets doctor_cure_flag ($CA5E-$CA69). A CON that is not equal to MAXCON sets doctor_heal_flag (con_is_full $0374 compares the two words for equality only), so a CON above MAXCON is offered healing too. When none of the three offers stands it goes back to doctor_ask ($CA7E), otherwise to doctor_menu.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CA5A: 1 while an exam is on offer to this patient, set by doctor_ask ($CA1F) and cleared once one has been paid for ($CBEB). Read here, at $CA75 (the offers), $CA98 (E)xam on the menu) and $CBCC (the E key).

Operand of the first ORA #imm, at $CA78: 1 while C)uring is on offer, set by doctor_offer when the exam has been done and the disease byte +$28 is non-zero ($CA66), cleared by doctor_ask ($CA23) and when the last disease is cured ($CBBD). Read at $CA8E (C)uring on the menu) and $CB59 (the C key).

Operand of the second ORA #imm, at $CA7A: 1 while H)ealing is on offer (CON not equal to MAXCON, set at $CA72), cleared by doctor_ask ($CA26) and when healing reaches MAXCON ($CB4B). Read at $CAA9 (H)ealing on the menu) and $CAD6 (the H key). The LDA and two ORAs leave A non-zero when any of the three offers stands.
P on the doctor's menu: moves every other member's cash to the patient (pool_cash $038F with A = doctor_patient, which ends with the patient selected) and shows the offers again (doctor_offer).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CA81: the patient's position in the party (1-7), stored at $CA3C after pick_member; read at $CAEC, $CB40, $CB50, $CBB4 and $CBC3 to select that member, redraw its roster line and pool the party's cash to it.

The doctor's menu: message 10 (code 4 clears the window, then "Well <name>, I would recommend:"), C)uring (message 13) while doctor_cure_flag is set, E)xam $ and the price at record +5 (message 11, print_byte $02F6) while doctor_exam_flag is set, H)ealing (message 12) while doctor_heal_flag is set; then flush_line ($0264) and the cash line (doctor_show_cash). Keys (wait_key $022F): left-arrow back to doctor_ask, P doctor_pool, H doctor_heal (only with the heal offer, $CAD6), C doctor_cure, E doctor_exam (each of those two checks its own flag); any other key is ignored.

Healing, one CON point for each payment: "Healing costs $<record +4> per CON point. You need to heal <n> points. Press Y to heal 1 point." (messages 14-16; n = MAXCON - CON as a 16-bit number, print_word $02F9, or "alot more", message 22, when the patient is not conscious, CON 0 or less, member_is_conscious $02BA), then the cash line. Keys: left-arrow back to doctor_offer (through the BEQ at $CB7E), P pools the cash to the patient ($CB50), Y pays record +4 (doctor_price, spend_cash $03CE; too little: doctor_no_money) and heals one point (heal_one $040A), and a second point free when CON has just become exactly 0, which would read as dead (con_is_zero, $CB38-$CB3D). The roster line is redrawn; while CON after the paid point is not equal to MAXCON (heal_one's carry, kept across the free point) the screen is shown again, otherwise doctor_heal_flag is cleared and the offers are shown again.

C)uring: the C key does nothing without doctor_cure_flag ($CBD1). Lists the patient's diseases (doctor_list_diseases with the disease byte +$28), "Enter # to cure at $<record +6> each." (messages 20, 21) and the cash line. Keys: left-arrow back to doctor_offer, P pools the cash to the patient ($CBC3), 1-8 a disease: ignored unless the patient has it; otherwise pays record +6 (spend_cash $03CE; too little: doctor_no_money), clears that bit of +$28 (doctor_cure_index, doctor_disease_bits) and redraws the roster line. With diseases left the list comes again; with none, doctor_cure_flag is cleared and the offers are shown again.

Operand of the LDX #imm at $CBA6: the disease being paid for, 0-7 (the digit key less one), stored at $CB99 once the patient is known to have it; it picks the mask in doctor_disease_bits whose bit is then cleared from +$28.

E)xam: the E key does nothing without doctor_exam_flag ($CBD1). Pays record +5 (doctor_price, spend_cash $03CE; too little: doctor_no_money), then shows either "You have no diseases." (message 17, with the (RETURN) wait of its code 6) or the list of the patient's diseases (doctor_list_diseases) and a (RETURN) wait (control code 6 through print_char_wrapped $0284). Clears doctor_exam_flag, which lets doctor_offer look at the diseases, and shows the offers again.

"You don't have enough money." (message 18, code 4 clearing the window first and the (RETURN) wait of code 6 after) and back to doctor_offer. Reached from healing, curing and the exam when spend_cash ($03CE) returns carry clear; nothing has been taken.

Lists the diseases in A (the disease byte +$28 of a character record): "You're inflicted with:" (message 19, whose code 4 clears the window), then for each set bit n (0-7, lowest first) a line "<n+1>> " and message n+1, the disease's name: 1 Radiation poisoning, 2 Wasteland Herpes, 3 Bug byte, 4 Sewer rot, 5 Desert dust, 6 Rabies, 7 D6, 8 D7 (the last two are placeholder names), each line ended by flush_line ($0264). $50 counts the bits; the digit is what the cure screen's keys take.
Price in $1C-$1E for spend_cash: the low byte from byte Y of the doctor's record at ($5F/$60) (Y = 4 healing, 5 the exam, 6 a cure), the two higher bytes 0.
Prints message A of the doctor's text block with direct output (output_direct $02FF), then as doctor_print. Used only for the cash line (doctor_show_cash).

Prints message A of the doctor's text block word-wrapped: selects output_wrapped ($0302), points $43/$44 at doctor_text ($CC78) and jumps to print_message ($0311). Every message of the module goes through here or doctor_print_direct; the greeting comes from the map's own block instead.

Masks $01, $02, $04, $08, $10, $20, $40, $80 for the diseases 0-7 of the disease byte +$28 (keys 1-8 on the cure screen): ANDed to test the chosen disease ($CB94), inverted and ANDed to clear it ($CBA8).

The cash line at the top of the text window: from column 14, row 2 (the cursor $23/$24) "P)ool Money = $" with direct output (message 24, whose code 3 clears the rest of the line), then the current character's cash, which is the patient's (cash_load $0392, print_long $02F0; the $30 = 8 set here print_long sets again itself).

Module 0's packed text block (5-bit codes read from the lowest bit up; work/text.py decodes it), first its 60-byte alphabet, codes 0-$29: space e o (end) t n RETURN a s i r d l h y u p m w c . g (code 4) b ) $ " (code 6) v : ' (code $0B, the name) x f ? = 7 6 1 , # (code 3); $2A-$3B hold $7F and are not used. Codes $1E (capital) and $1F (escape) are not letters, so the entries at $1E and $1F (' and code $0B) are reached as escape plus 0 and plus 1. doctor_print points $43/$44 here.

Seven offsets, each counted from this table at $CCB4, to the message groups of the doctor's text: $000E (group 0 at $CCC2), $002E ($CCE2), $0046 ($CCFA), $0077 ($CD2B), $00AA ($CD5E), $00FB ($CDAF), $0124 ($CDD8). Message n is in group n/4; find_message ($1E0E) decodes and drops the messages before it in its group.
Message group 0 (messages 0-3, one bit stream): 0 empty, never printed; 1 "Radiation poisoning"; 2 "Wasteland Herpes"; 3 "Bug byte" (the names of the diseases in bits 0-2 of +$28, listed as 1-3).
Message group 1 (messages 4-7): "Sewer rot", "Desert dust", "Rabies" and "D6", the names of the diseases in bits 3-6 of +$28 (D6 is a placeholder).

Message group 2 (messages 8-11): 8 "D7", the placeholder name of bit 7; 9 RETURN, "<name> is beyond my help.", RETURN and code 6 (a (RETURN) wait); 10 code 4 (clear the window), two RETURNs, a quoted "Well <name>, I would recommend:" and RETURN; 11 "E)xam $".
Message group 3 (messages 12-15): 12 RETURN, "H)ealing", RETURN; 13 RETURN, "C)uring"; 14 code 4, two RETURNs, "Healing costs $"; 15 " per CON point.", two RETURNs, "You need to heal ".

Message group 4 (messages 16-19): 16 " points. Press Y to heal 1 point." and RETURN; 17 code 4, "You have no diseases.", RETURN, code 6; 18 code 4, "You don't have enough money.", RETURN, code 6; 19 code 4, a quoted "You're inflicted with:" and two RETURNs.

Message group 5 (messages 20-23): 20 "Enter # to cure at $"; 21 " each." and RETURN; 22 "alot more", printed instead of the number of points to heal when the patient is not conscious; 23 "Who wants treatment?" and RETURN.

Message group 6, holding only message 24, the last: "P)ool Money = $" and code 3 (clear to the end of the line). Its end code finishes in bit 0 of $CDE5, the last byte of the block that is ever read. The byte after it, $CDE6 ($20), is the last value decoded from module 0's own packed bytes, from the stream's final four bits (code 1000, entry 0 of the value table); nothing reads it, and whether it was meant or is padding of the last byte is not known.

Not part of module 0, whose own bytes end at $CDE6. Its packed stream is 921 bytes, but the module directory gives the unpacker a window of four sectors (the entry's third byte), so it decodes on, with module 0's value table, into the stream that follows on the disk: module 1's on sides 1, 2 and 4 (on side 1 from track 25, logical sector 12, byte 153), module 2's on side 3, which is why side 3's copy differs from here on and ends at $CE5B. Nothing reads these bytes.
